System description:
# Case: Uber ATG automated test vehicle (Tempe, Arizona, 2018)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-19/03. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A modified Volvo XC90 SUV is used by Uber Advanced Technologies Group (ATG) to test an automated driving system (ADS) on public roads. The ADS is designed to drive the vehicle without human input in defined conditions, up to about 45 mph in this test program.

## Main parts
- Sensors: roof-mounted lidar, radar units and cameras covering the area around the vehicle.
- Perception: detects objects around the vehicle, classifies each one (for example vehicle, pedestrian, bicycle, other), and tracks it over time.
- Prediction: estimates where each tracked object will go next, using its class and recent movement.
- Planning and control: chooses a path and speed, and controls steering, throttle and braking.
- Vehicle: the Volvo factory driver-assistance features (such as forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking) are part of the base vehicle.

## People
- One vehicle operator sits in the driver seat. The operator is responsible for watching the road and taking over control when needed. The operator also uses a tablet-style interface to tag events and check system status.
- Other road users share the road: pedestrians, cyclists and other drivers. They are not aware of the test program.

## Operating context
Public multi-lane roads in an urban area, day and night, with posted speed limits, marked crosswalks, intersections and street lighting that varies by location.

goals.text: Conduct automated-driving-system tests on public roads.
Operate within the test program's defined conditions and speed limit.
Drive without human input when operating in defined conditions.
Navigate public roads.
Stay within the test program's speed limit of about 45 mph.
Sense the area around the vehicle using lidar, radar, and cameras.
Detect road users and other objects around the vehicle.
Classify detected objects, such as vehicles, pedestrians, and bicycles.
Track detected objects over time.
Estimate where each tracked object will move next using its class and recent movement.
Select a path and speed for the vehicle.
Control the vehicle's steering, throttle, and braking.
Execute the automated driving system's control inputs.
Provide forward collision warnings.
Apply automatic emergency braking when needed.
Watch the road while the automated driving system is operating.
Take over vehicle control when needed.
Check automated driving system status using the tablet-style interface.
Tag test events using the tablet-style interface.
Travel and cross the road safely.
Ride on the road safely.
Drive and share the road safely.

requirements.text: The system shall retain every sensor detection that could plausibly be a pedestrian, cyclist, or other road user as a tracked hazard until evidence rules it out, and shall command a conservative speed or stop when its presence cannot be resolved.

For each tracked road user, the system shall evaluate plausible deviations from the predicted trajectory, including entry into the vehicle's path, and shall select a speed and path that remain safe for those deviations.

The system shall limit speed so that, under the current measured visibility and road conditions, it can stop before the nearest distance at which an obstacle may become detectable; if it cannot, it shall slow or stop.
The system shall prevent event-tagging and other nonessential tablet interactions while the vehicle is moving, allowing them only when the vehicle is stopped in a safe location.

The system shall issue a takeover alert while sufficient validated response time remains for the operator to intervene and shall initiate a minimum-risk maneuver if the operator does not acknowledge and take control within the validated takeover-response interval.
When a road user's classification is uncertain or unstable, the system shall use the most safety-critical plausible classification for prediction and planning until the classification is resolved.

When a road-user track is lost, fragmented, or affected by sensor disagreement, the system shall preserve its possible location and motion as an uncertainty region and plan to avoid that region until the road user is reacquired or ruled out.

The system shall continuously monitor all defined operating-condition limits, including visibility and traffic complexity, and shall slow to a stop or otherwise enter a defined minimum-risk state whenever a limit is exceeded or cannot be reliably assessed.

Before and during ADS operation, the system shall verify that automatic emergency braking is available and effective; if it is unavailable or ineffective, the ADS shall not begin or continue operation unless it can meet the same validated collision-avoidance safety objective without that feature.

The system shall account for pedestrians emerging from occlusion at any location alongside the roadway, including between parked vehicles, by limiting speed to one that permits stopping within the available sight distance.
